name: GroupGenerator_init
reason: Its only entry, unicodeobj-format-group-loop, refutes 'rounds <= digits + 1', which CPython never promises: a zero-padded grouped field of width 40 needs about 13 groups, so the counterexample is required output, and the real defect (no interrupt before a doomed allocation) is not what the Lean statement says.

name: GroupGenerator_next
reason: group-loop is not a promised property (see GroupGenerator_init), and FloatGroupingOnlyInserts only says that removing separators restores the text, so a generator that always returns 0 (no grouping at all) still satisfies every theorem.

name: InsertThousandsGrouping_fill
reason: GroupDigits and FloatGroupingOnlyInserts are both 'filter out the separator, get the digits back', which holds for a fill that writes no separator or puts it in the wrong place, so nothing pins where separators and zeros go.

name: _PyUnicode_InsertThousandsGrouping
reason: group-digits and float-grouping hold for any routine that inserts separators anywhere or not at all (only the count = length relation is checked), and group-loop is a refutation of a bound CPython never promised, so separator placement, the min_width zero padding and the post-loop branch are never pinned.

name: unknown_presentation_type
reason: StrFormatErrors states formatStrAdvanced s [t] = .error (unknownPresentationType t "str"), with the model function itself on the right-hand side, so the theorem holds for any definition of it and neither message branch (%c for 33..127, \x%x otherwise) is pinned.

name: invalid_thousands_separator_type
reason: It is only checked on four concrete specs (',', '_', ',s', '_s', all with type 's') whose right-hand side is the model function itself, so the \x%x branch is never reached and the message is not pinned.

name: invalid_comma_and_underscore
reason: It is only rfl on two concrete specs ([44,95], [95,44]) whose right-hand side is the same constant; the precision-side call sites (:511, :523) never run in any theorem.

name: get_integer
reason: StrFormatDoc assumes accum 0 wd <= ssizeMax and uses ASCII digits only, so the 'Too many decimal digits in format string' overflow branch and non-ASCII decimal digits (Py_UNICODE_TODECIMAL) are assumed away.

name: is_alignment_token
reason: StrFormatDoc only needs isAlignmentToken align = true for align in < > ^, so `fun _ => true` passes; '=' and the false branch are never constrained.

name: is_sign_element
reason: The only use in the proof is isSignElement (d+48) = false for a digit, so `fun _ => false` satisfies the theorem and the sign branch is never exercised.

name: parse_internal_render_format_spec
reason: Its only entry fixes the spec to fill+align+ASCII width[.precision]+'s' with width <= sys.maxsize, so the sign, z, #, zero-padding and separator branches and every error path (missing precision, invalid specifier, separator validation, digit overflow) are outside the theorem.

name: calc_padding
reason: StrFormatDoc requires wd != [], so the width < 0 branch (precision without width, e.g. format('abcdef', '.2')) never runs, and a calc_padding returning any lpad for width < 0 still passes.

name: fill_padding
reason: fillPadding is replicate l ++ content ++ replicate r, and StrFormatDoc pins it against the independent docFormat for <, > and ^ at every width and string.

name: calc_number_widths
reason: Its entries are FloatWidthIsMinimum and IntWidthIsMinimum ('len >= width'), which hold for padding on the wrong side, a wrong sign, or digits dropped and replaced by fill, so the sign switch, the alignment switch and n_min_width are not pinned by them.

name: fill_number
reason: Its entries are only the width-is-minimum theorems, which a fill_number writing width fill characters and nothing else would satisfy; field order, toupper and the decimal and fraction placement are not pinned.

name: free_locale_info
reason: Only Py_XDECREFs strings it created and frees a strdup'd buffer; the exact str objects it drops run no finalizer, so no-behaviour applies.

name: format_string_internal
reason: StrFormatDoc never sets sign, z, # or '=' (fill+align is fixed and align is in < > ^), so the four ValueError branches (:1110-1144) are never exercised by its entry, and a version without them passes.

name: format_long_internal
reason: IntFormatAsStr only covers type 'd' with fill+align+width, so the 'c' branch, bases b/o/x/X, #, sign, separators, the fast path and the precision and z errors are never exercised by this row's entry.

name: format_float_internal
reason: floatBuf (the type, precision and flags setup at :1409-1458: '' to 'r' with ADD_DOT_0, 'n' to 'g', '%' to f*100, default precision) appears on both sides of FloatSpecLayout and FloatFastSlowAgree, so a version passing 'e' for 'f' or ignoring precision satisfies every entry.

name: format_complex_internal
reason: Mirrored in source order; ComplexPartsCompose pins the typed path against float formatting of the parts, ComplexOmittedTypeIsRepr pins the omitted type against complex_repr, and FloatComplexErrors pins the three refusals in order.

name: _PyUnicode_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: formatStrAdvanced returns the value for an empty spec, but for a str subclass C calls format_obj -> PyObject_Str (:1806-1807), which can run __str__ and raise, and the error uses Py_TYPE(obj)->tp_name, which the model fixes to 'str'; its entry also covers only the fill+align+width+'s' spec.

name: _PyLong_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: The empty-spec result is a free parameter emptyStr in place of _PyLong_FormatWriter vs format_obj (:1840-1843), PyNumber_Float on an int subclass can call a user __float__ but the model only has an overflow check, and the entry only exercises type 'd'.

name: _PyFloat_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: The empty spec is modelled as float_repr, but C calls format_obj -> PyObject_Str (:1900), which for a float subclass runs its __repr__/__str__ (can differ or raise); the type name in errors is fixed to 'float' rather than tp_name.

name: _PyComplex_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: The empty spec is modelled as complex_repr, but C calls format_obj -> PyObject_Str (:1939), which runs a complex subclass's __repr__/__str__; the type name in errors is fixed to 'complex'.
